validated_results.title: Urinary 6-sulfatoxymelatonin Levels and Prostate Cancer Risk among Men in the Multiethnic Cohort.
validated_results.journal: Cancer epidemiology, biomarkers & prevention : a publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, cosponsored by the American Society of Preventive Oncology
validated_results.reason: Prospective nested case-control study evaluating urinary 6-sulfatoxymelatonin levels and risk of incident prostate cancer with multivariable-adjusted effect estimates.

cases.excerpt: We conducted a nested case-control study, 1,263 prostate cancer cases and 2,346 controls, sampled from participants in the Multiethnic Cohort Study with pre-diagnostic urine samples assayed for 6-sulfatoxymelatonin, the primary melatonin metabolite. Conditional logistic regression was used to examine the association between melatonin levels and the development of prostate cancer outcomes (all incident cases, advanced, lethal, high-grade, and aggressive), overall and by race/ethnicity.

effect_size.excerpt: Neither unadjusted nor adjusted models showed an association between urinary melatonin and overall prostate cancer (OR continuous : 1.01, 0.93-1.09; OR Q4vsQ1 : 1.06, 0.85-1.32).

comparison.excerpt: Melatonin jackknife residuals and the derived quartiles were used as a continuous and categorical exposure, respectively.

timing.excerpt: selected among men who contributed a pre-diagnostic urine sample between 1996-2005. Incident prostate cancer cases along with respective tumor characteristics were identified through the National Cancer Institute’s Surveillance, Epidemiology and End Results (SEER) Program in Hawaii and California.

continent.excerpt: Incident prostate cancer cases along with respective tumor characteristics were identified through the National Cancer Institute’s Surveillance, Epidemiology and End Results (SEER) Program in Hawaii and California.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Urine samples were assayed for 6-sulfatoxymelatonin (the primary metabolite of urinary melatonin) using the melatonin sulfate enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (IBL International, Toronto, ON, Canada)
